text:
sam: Quick sync on adding a "coldstart token" layer to the autoscaler. Goal: prevent noisy traffic from burning generic burst credits and isolate warmup actions (VM start + model load).

maria: short question: why a new token vs tagging burst credits as "for-warmup"?

sam: two reasons: 1) semantic clarity for billing/chargeback, 2) separate refill/limits so sustained traffic can't deplete warmup budget.

alex: Can we see a config sketch?

sam: sketch below:
```yaml
autoscaling:
  mode: hybrid
  coldstart_tokens:
    initial: 3
    refill_interval: 1h
    max: 24
  predictive:
    enabled: true
    lookback: 5m
  reactive:
    tail_latency_threshold_ms: 250
    max_emergency_spend_per_month: 10
```

jen: billing question: who bears prewarm cost while weights are streaming?

sam: proposal: predictive prewarms charged to tenant (reservation); reactive prewarms get subsidized allowance based on plan, then billed if over. Refund if operator aborts quickly.

kai: refunds create accounting complexity. Alternative: predictive = reservation (no refunds), reactive = best-effort subsidized pool capped per-tenant. If over cap, deny or bill.

maria: tie subsidized caps to customer tier. Also need operator guardrails so predictive scheduling can't reserve whole cluster.

alex: operator API should include an AdmitIntent envelope with estimates: required_gpus, token_spend_estimate, model_hash, ttl_s. Example (dry-run friendly).

sam: yes. AdmitIntent proto will let operator accept, delay, or reject with reason codes (CAPACITY, SAFETY, QUOTA).

jen: observability: metrics we need: cold_tokens_used_total, cold_token_refills_total, predictive_prewarms, reactive_prewarms, prewarm_evictions. Dashboards and alerts when predictive_prewarms > 40% headroom.

kai: rollout plan: opt-in tenants -> canary group -> tiered enablement by plan. Operator should have a cluster-wide kill-switch for predictive spends.

maria: pool compatibility: reserved pools honor predictive prewarms; shared pools require operator approval and stricter caps. Add mapping in policy layer.

alex: edge-case: model swap during prewarm (wasted work). Include expected_model_hash in AdmitIntent, operator verifies at start and can cancel if mismatch. Also add prewarm TTL to auto-release.

sam: add dry_run flag to admit API so we can simulate impacts without carving resources. Response should include estimated_cost, estimated_prewarm_time_s, and reject_reasons.

infra-bot: staging-note: implemented atomic admit dry_run and metrics emit for predictive_prewarms. Canary run 1/20 tenants, no regressions so far.

jen: next step: short RFC addendum + proto for AdmitIntent + sample PromQL queries + rollout checklist. I'll draft ops playbook bits.

sam: I'll open a PR with config schema and admit proto. Thanks! :rocket:
